# PreviewLayer

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Imaging` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public readonly struct PreviewLayer : IEquatable<PreviewLayer>
```

One reference layer in a stack preview: which ingredient, which of its variants, and the color to draw it in.

## Constructors

### PreviewLayer(LoadedIngredient, string, string?, RolledColor?) { #m-ctor-nfty-core-formats-loadedingredient-system-string-9720be }

```csharp
public PreviewLayer(LoadedIngredient Ingredient, string VariantId, string? ColorSpec, RolledColor? Rolled = null);
```

**Parameters**

- `Ingredient` (`LoadedIngredient`) - The layer to draw. Its images stay owned by it — [`StackPreview.Render()`](Nfty.Core.Imaging.StackPreview.md#m-render-nfty-core-model-dimensions-system-collections-g-7bf0b3) renders through [`VariantPreview`](Nfty.Core.Imaging.VariantPreview.md), which never hands out a borrowed image, so nothing here ever disposes what an ingredient owns.
- `VariantId` (`string`) - Which variant to draw. [`StackPreview.PickVariant()`](Nfty.Core.Imaging.StackPreview.md#m-pickvariant-nfty-core-formats-loadedingredient) is the deterministic default when the caller has no opinion.
- `ColorSpec` (`string?`) - A prefixed color spec (`hex:`, `rgb:`, `hsl:`, `hsv:`) for a Dynamic or Static layer; ignored by a Custom one, which is composited as-is and never colorized. Which kinds need one is [`VariantPreview.NeedsColor()`](Nfty.Core.Imaging.VariantPreview.md#m-needscolor-nfty-core-formats-loadedingredient)'s answer and the requirement is `VariantPreview.Render`'s to enforce — restating either here would be a second copy of a rule that has exactly one owner.
- `Rolled` (`RolledColor?`) - The rolled hue and saturation, unrounded — set for a layer whose color was *rolled* rather than authored. **When present it is what gets drawn, and `ColorSpec` becomes display only.** Both exist because they answer different questions. A spec is what a human reads, pastes and re-runs; a [`RolledColor`](../nfty-ticket/Nfty.Core.Generation.RolledColor.md) is what generation actually hands the colorizer. Every spec resolves through 8-bit RGB, so a rolled hue that fell between two representable colors cannot be spelled exactly — carrying only the string put the preview a rounding step off the asset it claims to show. Carrying both keeps the printed spec readable AND the rendered pixel exact. Null for Static (an author-written spec, resolved identically by generation, so already exact) and for Custom (no color at all).

The rolled hue and saturation, unrounded — set for a layer whose color was *rolled* rather than authored. **When present it is what gets drawn, and `ColorSpec` becomes display only.**

Both exist because they answer different questions. A spec is what a human reads, pastes and re-runs; a [`RolledColor`](../nfty-ticket/Nfty.Core.Generation.RolledColor.md) is what generation actually hands the colorizer. Every spec resolves through 8-bit RGB, so a rolled hue that fell between two representable colors cannot be spelled exactly — carrying only the string put the preview a rounding step off the asset it claims to show. Carrying both keeps the printed spec readable AND the rendered pixel exact.

Null for Static (an author-written spec, resolved identically by generation, so already exact) and for Custom (no color at all).

## Methods

### Render() { #m-render }

```csharp
public Image<Rgba32> Render();
```

Renders this layer through [`VariantPreview`](Nfty.Core.Imaging.VariantPreview.md): the rolled color when there is one (it is exact; the spec beside it is only its 8-bit spelling), the spec otherwise. The one place that choice is made, for the stack preview and the CLI's `model` alike.

**Returns.** The rendered layer; the caller owns and disposes it.
